source.title: Belfast Newsletter, 8 June 1964, p. 9 ("Hillsborough Rural District Council: notice of result of elections, 1964")

source.check: the returning officer’s notice of result in the Belfast News-Letter of 8 June 1964, with the counts from the report of 5 June.

note: Triennial election of Hillsborough Rural District Council, polled Thursday 4 June 1964. Hillsborough, Maze and Anahilt were contested and the other thirteen divisions were returned unopposed. Addresses and occupations printed with the names are not reproduced (privacy rule; gap-fill 6 Nov 2026). Returned unopposed.
correctionNote: Corrected from the page images of the Belfast News-Letter, 5 June 1964, p. 2 and 8 June 1964, p. 9 (council-audit, Nov 2026): the round note now says Hillsborough, Maze and Anahilt were contested (it said Maze recorded a poll for a single candidate; the defeated Maze candidate had been filed under Hillsborough). Renamed from 'Ballyworphy' to Ballyworfy (19 Nov 2026, w19-tidy, the owner's decision 4 of 19 Nov 2026: a division filed under two spellings takes its official name, and each round keeps the spelling it was filed under as Constituency_Name_As_Printed): the 1911 DED map (Hillsborough Rural District) and the Northern Ireland DED maps of 1921-69 name the DED Ballyworfy; the rounds were filed as Ballyworfy (1924, 1930, 1933, 1949, 1952, 1955, 1967); Ballyworphy (1927, 1936, 1939, 1946, 1958, 1961, 1964). This round was filed as 'Ballyworphy', kept as Constituency_Name_As_Printed; the old address (ballyworphy) answers with a redirect to this one.
